subject: Re: ACME - Rerank model fit & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: ACME discovery follow-up: rerank & evals

Hi Jordan — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can get a focused evaluation in place: 

Recap
- Goal: improve search relevance on product & docs pages with a reranking layer; primary KPI is NDCG@10 and secondary is MRR for navigational queries.
- Dataset size: ~500k queries historically, with click labels available for ~120k.
- Latency SLO: 50–80ms p95 for the rerank step (batched inference acceptable).

What Redwood recommends for an initial fit/eval
1) Candidate reranker models to validate: rwd-rerank-small-v1 (dense), rwd-rerank-lora-v1 (parameter-efficient), and open-rerank-3b-quant (for higher accuracy / higher cost tradeoff).
2) Eval metrics: NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, precision@k, and a calibrated click-model lift. Please confirm you want NDCG@10 as the primary metric.
3) Prompt set & synthetic edge cases: we'll use a focused prompt set of 1k queries + 200 adversarial/paraphrase cases. I can share the prompt_set_v2.jsonl once you confirm.
4) A/B plan: start with an offline holdout + shadow traffic (1%) then a 10% online canary comparing current production rank vs Redwood reranker for 2 weeks.

Data we need from you
- 1) A representative sample of 20k query-candidate pairs with click labels (anonymized).
- 2) Current baseline ranking scores (if available).
- 3) A list of sensitive query filters (PII) to exclude.

Next steps
- If you can drop the sample to the Drive link I shared in the call, we’ll run a 3–5 day offline eval and return an NDCG/MRR report.
- I’ll follow up with a quick eval plan and a proposed A/B schedule.

I’m looping in Rishi and Connor for the technical canary/runbook. If you’re good with the plan, can we schedule a 30-min technical workshop this week to confirm data format and traffic routing?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME discovery follow-up: rerank & evals

Marissa — this is great, thanks for the clear recap. Confirm NDCG@10 as primary. We can provide the 20k sample and baseline scores by EOD tomorrow. A couple of clarifications: 

- For latency, the 50–80ms p95 is for the rerank-only step (we do candidate retrieval separately). We can tolerate higher p95 for heavy queries if it improves quality, but we'd like the default path to stay under 100ms.
- Regarding model variants: cost is a concern; open-rerank-3b-quant may be acceptable for a subset of high-value queries.

I dropped a link to the sample in the shared Drive folder you gave during the call: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AcmeSampleDump (attached). Also attaching a small baseline.csv with our current system scores.

Can do a workshop Tue or Wed morning PT.

—Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME discovery follow-up: rerank & evals

Thanks Jordan — got the sample and baseline.csv. I started a quick offline run this morning and attaching preliminary results (acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr.xlsx) — these are early and on the 20k sample only. Highlights: 

- rwd-rerank-small-v1: NDCG@10 = 0.421, MRR = 0.58 (Δ +6.2% NDCG vs baseline)
- rwd-rerank-lora-v1: NDCG@10 = 0.437, MRR = 0.60 (Δ +9.1%)
- open-rerank-3b-quant: NDCG@10 = 0.449, MRR = 0.615 (Δ +12.8%)

Notes & quality/regression flags
- We observed a small regression on navigational queries for a subset of short queries (top-1 swap); that’s expected for more aggressive rerankers and should be covered in the promptset adversarial tests.
- Latency estimates (p95) from our local bench: small-v1 ~22ms (CPU + quantized GPU path), lora-v1 ~35ms, open-3b-quant ~120ms (so open-3b likely needs dedicated capacity or selective routing).

Attachments & links
- acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr.xlsx (attached) — full per-query slice breakdown and NDCG/MRR by intent
- prompt_set_v2.jsonl — (shared Drive) contains the 1k canonical + 200 adversarial cases: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmE-Rerank-Evals

Recommended next steps
1) Run the adversarial prompt set (1.2k) against top two candidates (small-v1 and lora-v1) to validate regression cases.
2) If lora-v1 holds for the short-query slice, propose a 10% online canary for 2 weeks comparing prod -> rerank(lora-v1). Monitor NDCG@10, top-1 precision, and navigational regression rate.
3) For the open-3b option, recommend selective routing: only route queries classified as high-value (50% of checkout/search flows) to open-3b while falling back to lora-v1 for others. That avoids full-cost rollout.

Jordan — are you able to accept the canary configuration above? If yes, we’ll draft an A/B runbook (metrics, alert thresholds, rollback triggers) and schedule the workshop tomorrow morning PT.

—Marissa

Rishi / Connor — looping you both in to align on the A/B runbook and capacity. Key ask: can we support the recommended 10% canary for lora-v1 and selective routing for open-3b-quant? Notes: 

- Expected traffic: ~4k qps peak for candidate retrieval; rerank step will be batched (target batch sizes 8–16). Canary 10% ~400 qps peak.
- Latency target for canary path: p95 < 100ms (includes added batch wait time). We should set an alert at 120ms and automatic rollback if navigational regression > 1.5% absolute.
- Monitoring: need NDCG@10 rolling window (1h/24h), top-1 precision, MRR and a small set of synthetic adversarial tests to run nightly. Can Redwood provide a per-route eval dashboard (token & request cost) and auto-delta alerts?

Connor — can you draft the serving config (batching, model selection rules, fallback to lora-v1) and estimate required vGPU hours for a 2-week canary on Dedicated? Rishi — can you own the A/B runbook (metrics, thresholds, rollback) and set up dashboards/traces?

I’ll prepare the runbook draft and send to Jordan once you both say this is feasible. Also I’ll add HubSpot deal ACME-2026-001 and propose Wed 10:00 AM PT for the workshop.

Thanks —
